{{family name hatnote|Kim||lang=Korean}}

'''Kim Jihn-eui''' ({{Korean|hangul=김진의}}; born July 30, 1946) is a South Korean [[theoretical physicist]]. His research interests concentrate on [[particle physics]] and [[cosmology]] and has many contributions to the field, most notably the suggestion of the invisible axion.

==Birth and education==
Kim was born in [[Gurye]], [[South Jeolla Province]] in 1946. He graduated from [[Kyunggi High School]] and earned his bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from [[Seoul National University]] in 1971. He earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[particle physics]] from [[University of Rochester]] in 1975. He became a research associate at [[Brown University]] from 1975 to 1977 and worked as a research investigator at [[University of Pennsylvania]] to 1980. Then he was appointed to assistant professor of Seoul National University in 1980 and had been there until retirement in 2011. Afterwards he took a position at [[Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology]] in [[Gwangju]]. Currently he is distinguished professor and eminent scholar at [[Kyung Hee University]].

He was also a professor in School of Physics at [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1998 to 1999 and held many inviting positions from other institutions including [[CERN]], [[University of Michigan]], [[Harvard University]] and [[University of Bonn]].

==Research==
Kim's research is focused on the elementary particle theory and particle cosmology.
He suggested the invisible axion model known as the [[Peccei–Quinn theory#Invisible axion models|KSVZ]] (Kim–Shifman–Vainshtein–Zakharov) model, which provides a solution to the [[strong CP problem]] in the [[Standard Model]].<ref>{{cite journal
|author=Jihn E. Kim
|title= Weak Interaction Singlet and Strong CP Invariance
|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.
|volume=4
|pages=103–107
|year=1979
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.103
|bibcode=1979PhRvL..43..103K
|issue=2
}}</ref>
He also advocated that the [[axino]], the supersymmetric dual of [[axion]], can be a strong candidate of [[dark matter]] of our universe
and contended that it might have played an important role in the formation of galaxies and may offer a significant part of the current energy density of the universe. 
His review about the neutral current gave a good understanding of the [[Electroweak interaction|Glashow–Salam–Weinberg model]] to the field.<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=P. Langacker |author2=Jihn E. Kim |author3=M. Levine |author4=H.H. Williams |author5=D.P. Sidhu |title=The Weak Neutral Current: A Determination Of Its Structure And An Analysis Of The Error Due To Theoretical And Experimental Uncertainties
|journal=Bergen 1979, Proceedings, Neutrino '79
|volume=1
|pages=276
|year=1979
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Jihn E. Kim |author2=Paul Langacker |author3=M. Levine |author4=H.H. Williams |title=A Theoretical and Experimental Review of the Weak Neutral Current: A Determination of Its Structure and Limits on Deviations from the Minimal SU(2)-L x U(1) Electroweak Theory
|journal=Rev. Mod. Phys.
|volume=53
|pages=211
|year=1981
|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.53.211
|bibcode=1981RvMP...53..211K
|issue=2
}}</ref>
With H. P. Nilles, he formulated and presented the solution of the μ problem in [[supergravity]], 
then he led the calculation of the cosmological effect of the [[gravitino]].<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Johm Ellis |author2=Jihn E. Kim |author3=D. V. Nanopoulos |title=Cosmological gravitino regeneration and decay
|journal=Phys. Lett. B
|volume=145
|pages=181
|year=1984
|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(84)90334-4
|issue=3–4
|bibcode = 1984PhLB..145..181E |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/152555 }}</ref>
From the collapse effect of the supergraviton which interacts much weaker than a light axion or axino,
Kim obtained the upper limit of the reheating temperature of the universe 10<sup>9</sup>GeV and that made an early contribution 
of the field of cosmological research about heavy and weak interacting particles.<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Laura Covi |author2=Jihn E. Kim |author3=Leszek Roszkowski |title=Axinos as Cold Dark Matter
|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.
|volume=82
|pages=4180–4183
|year=1999
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.4180
|bibcode=1999PhRvL..82.4180C
|issue=21
|arxiv = hep-ph/9905212 |s2cid=119362674 }}</ref>
He also did the first attempt to get the Standard Model from the [[superstring theory]].
He contributed to the development of standard model from the higher-dimensional theories by reducing the dimensions of [[orbifold]]
and was absorbed in the [[cosmological constant]] problem and gave a clue of the solution of it in 5d [[spacetime]].

==Honors and awards==
* 1987: [[Korea Science Award]]
* 1992: [[Ho-Am Prize]]
* 2001: [[Humboldt Prize]]
* 2003: [[Top Scientist and Technologist Award of Korea]]<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.bosa.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=30655 |script-title=ko:김규원 교수 '최고과학기술인상' 수상 |author= 김상일 |date= 16 April 2003 |website= 의학신문 |publisher= |access-date= 16 November 2023 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref>
